scope: CBSE Class 6 Science · Curiosity · Chapter 8 · A Journey through States of Water
claimBoundary: Deterministic readiness validation using synthetic learner scenarios only. This is not a live student study, school pilot, efficacy trial, attainment claim, weather-forecasting validation, laboratory safety certification or permission for hazardous heating, steam, ingestion or outdoor collection activities.
passRule: Every scenario must map to an implemented Chapter 8 topic, a Kiki misconception/remediation path, at least one linked reasoning or mastery assessment, a privacy-safe learner action and an observable mastery criterion while preserving the no-boiling, no-steam-exposure, no-flame/hot-plate/sealed-heating, no-ingestion and evidence-limited model boundaries.

scenarios.need: Learner treats ice, liquid water and water vapour as different substances rather than different physical states of water.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Sort supplied state cards for ice, liquid water and water vapour, then state what remains the same and what observable state properties change without heating any sample.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly identifies unfamiliar solid/liquid/gas water examples as the same substance in different states and supports each state label with shape, flow or container evidence.

scenarios.need: Learner calls visible white mist 'water vapour' and assumes the gaseous state must be visible.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use supplied diagrams to separate invisible water vapour from visible condensed liquid droplets and explain why a visible cloud/mist is not direct visual evidence of gaseous water itself.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Consistently distinguishes invisible water vapour from visible condensed droplets in unfamiliar diagrams without proposing steam generation or hot-vapour exposure.

scenarios.need: Learner says evaporation only happens when water boils or says dried water has disappeared from existence.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Analyse room-temperature drying evidence cards and trace liquid water to dispersed water vapour, explicitly separating evaporation from boiling.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly identifies evaporation below boiling conditions and explains that water changes state and disperses rather than ceasing to exist.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes droplets on the outside of an intact sealed cold bottle must have leaked through the bottle wall.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare supplied evidence for a sealed intact cold container and surrounding air, then test which explanation—leakage or condensation—better fits the observations without opening, heating or freezing anything.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Uses the sealed/intact evidence to explain outside droplets as condensation of surrounding water vapour and identifies what evidence would be needed before claiming leakage.

scenarios.need: Learner proposes boiling water, using a kettle/flame/hot plate, heating a sealed container or placing a hand near steam to demonstrate a state change.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Reject the hazardous plan and replace it with supplied before/after diagrams, room-temperature evaporation observations or adult-provided ice/cold-surface evidence that answers the same state-change question.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Identifies each heating/steam hazard, rejects it as unnecessary and selects a lower-risk evidence source while still naming the correct state change.

scenarios.need: Learner changes several factors at once when comparing evaporation and then claims one factor caused the whole difference.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Redesign a supplied comparison so only one important factor changes while starting water amount, timing and other relevant conditions remain similar; interpret supplied measurements only.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Constructs a fair comparison, identifies the changed factor and controls, and writes a conclusion limited to the recorded conditions rather than a universal causal claim.

scenarios.need: Learner turns a simple evaporation/condensation classroom model into a complete explanation of clouds or a weather forecast.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use a supplied environmental-water diagram to identify what the model represents and list at least one atmospheric factor or complexity that the simple model does not capture.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains the useful evaporation/condensation connection while explicitly stating that the model is incomplete and cannot by itself provide a weather forecast.

scenarios.need: Learner needs offline water-state practice without uploading photos/location, drinking test water, climbing to collect samples or using heat to accelerate evaporation.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Complete cached text, diagrams and supplied data locally to classify states, identify state changes and interpret a fair evaporation comparison without sensors, uploads, ingestion, climbing or heat sources.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Completes the offline synthetic task using supplied evidence only, applies the water-state concepts accurately and avoids personal-data disclosure and hazardous collection/heating/ingestion methods.
